correctness.rationale: For a subspace W, WW=span{B(x,y)u}; closure is equivalent to u in W or B|W=0. Containment of u contributes a Gaussian coefficient; totally isotropic W contributes a finite-orthogonal polar-space T_r; an isotropic u creates the quotient overlap in u-perp/<u>. Counting isotropic lines by quadratic Gauss sums and flags by incidence reproduces the given product formula, including nonsplit maximal Witt index and zero-dimensional boundaries. In dimension two a height-two atom lattice is modular, distributive iff <=2 atoms. For n>=3 a hyperbolic pair and isotropic lines U,X outside Z=<u,U> construct the strict modular-law violation. The n=3 q=3 identity-form counts are [1,5,4,1] for anisotropic u and [1,4,4,1] for isotropic u; independent closure enumeration checked 480 subspaces across four q=3 cases. This is a proof reconstruction, not reliance on finite verification alone.

This is more than a textbook property check even though individual Gaussian/polar counts are classical.
